newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Milburn sees bounce in NZ building by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Milburn sees bounce in NZ building by 1998.

text.p: The outgoing chairman of building materials group Milburn New Zealand Limited said on Friday he believed the outlook for the construction market remained sound despite some expected softness.

Chairman Bob Stannard told the company's AGM that Milburn could expect "a period of softness in some of its markets, followed by a rise in demand as confidence returned and economic growth strengthened again".

"A number of large projects which are at the planning stage are expected to commence later this year or in 1998," Stannard added, noting government and local authority expenditure was also likely to grow.
Stannard stepped down at the meeting as he had reached retiring age. He has been replaced by Michael Robinson, while Rex Loach will replace Stannard on the board.
Milburn is 73 percent owned by Holderbank Financiere, the Swiss-based international cement giant.
